components.name: Analysis-only Moreau envelope
components.operation: Compare x_{t+1} to the analytical point prox_{phi/rho_bar}(x_t), without computing that point in the Algorithm.
components.requires: phi=f+iota_X; rho_bar>rho>=0; Assumption A and exact Euclidean projection.
transfer_checks: Approximate or non-Euclidean projection requires a new argument.
A bounded-variance Oracle alone does not supply the full second-moment assumption.
A different output rule or stationarity metric needs a separate performance argument.

content.family: Projected stochastic subgradient with Moreau-envelope analysis

limitations.statement: Performance concerns the stepsize-weighted randomized output and the Moreau-gradient metric; it does not establish last-iterate or high-probability guarantees.
No unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound or optimality claim is extracted.

performance_links.scope_note: Theorem 3.1 Eq.(3.3)–(3.5) under the complete assumptions of the attached Theorem record.

variants.cost: Direct accounting of the literal inclusive loop: T+1 independent samples, T+1 stochastic subgradient queries, T+1 exact projections, and T+1 vector updates. Projection computational cost is separate and is not bounded in the source theorem. The displayed retain-all implementation stores T+1 query points and samples a categorical output index; this implementation bookkeeping is not a source runtime theorem. No function-value, envelope-gradient or prox_{lambda phi} query is used.
variants.name: Algorithm 3.1 with r=iota_X
variants.output: Return x_R in X. It is a randomized query point, not an average and not necessarily x_T or x_{T+1}. Under constant steps the output distribution is uniform on {0,...,T}.
public_inputs: Nonempty closed convex X and an exact Euclidean projection routine
Finite integer horizon T>=0 and deterministic positive steps alpha_0,...,alpha_T
Fresh-sample stochastic subgradient routine G satisfying Assumption A
For constant-horizon tuning, any gamma>0; no gap estimate is needed to execute that choice
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,T, independently sample xi_t from P, query g_t=G(x_t,xi_t), then set x_{t+1}=proj_X(x_t-alpha_t*g_t). After this loop draw R from {0,...,T}, using additional randomness with conditional probabilities P(R=t | trajectory)=alpha_t/S, where S=sum_{i=0}^T alpha_i.
variants.requirements: f:R^d->R is rho-weakly convex, rho>=0; X is nonempty closed convex. On open U containing X, G is measurable and E G(x,xi) belongs to partial f(x) for all x in U. Fresh iid xi are available and E||G(x,xi)||^2<=L^2 for all x in X, with finite L>=0. Exact projection onto X is available. The finite attained minimum condition used by the attached performance record is additional to merely executing the recurrence.
variants.state_and_initialization: Initialize x_0 to the supplied feasible point. Retain the query points x_0,...,x_T for the final weighted draw. No objective value or Moreau envelope evaluation initializes the method.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Run the fixed horizon t=0,...,T inclusive. The projected Theorem 3.1 admits every deterministic positive stepsize sequence, with no stepsize upper bound. Its Eq.(3.5) specialization uses alpha_t=gamma/sqrt(T+1), gamma>0, and rho>0 for the envelope parameter 1/(2rho). This is not an adaptive stationarity stopping test.
